dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation

evidence.note: Read all four graph files, extracted |V|/|E| for both pairs, identified node-naming conventions (integer IDs vs gene names), and probed environment (no networkx/numpy/scipy, no network access, gcc available) before committing.
Computed the reference alignment's baseline S3 = 0.248 and recognized NC is measured against it — a genuine baseline-quantification orientation move (anchor 8/10 trait).
Identified the exact structural signal S3 rewards (Ea=11063 vs E2_aligned=39556), deriving that E2_al must drop to reach 0.55 — pinpointing the lever each threshold rewards.

Named known alignment methods (GRAAL, MAGNA++, SPINAL, IsoRank) but never researched/evaluated them (no internet); noticed differing per-deliverable constraints and used reference-seeding for NC while optimizing S3 for the yeast pair.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it characterized both pairs' sizes/format/naming, inspected the reference alignment, and picked reasoned approaches per deliverable. It also displays several anchor-8/10 traits — quantifying the baseline reference S3 (0.248), identifying the precise structural signal each threshold rewards (Ea vs E2_al), and recognizing the differing per-deliverable constraints with reference-seeding as the NC lever. However, it did no genuine method research (methods were named but never evaluated against instance sizes/runtime, partly due to no network access) and lacked full upfront degree-distribution characterization, which keeps it short of 8. This places the observed level at 7.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones

evidence.note: Ordered pipeline: load_graph.py (parser, verified against header counts) → align_utils.py (S3 scorer, produced reference S3=0.248) → greedy_align.py baseline. Scorer built and measured before any optimization — sensible sequencing.

Explicitly separated the two deliverables with their distinct numeric done-criteria: 'DM-HS pair only needs S3 >= 0.32 (no NC); yeast needs S3>=0.55 AND NC>=0.30 vs reference.' Treated them as separate goals throughout.

Milestones carry concrete numeric done-checks tied to thresholds: derived intermediate targets like 'need E2_al ≈ 11950 with Ea ≈ 9940 for S3=0.55' and 'Ea from 6518 to ~12000 for DM-HS 0.32', showing quantified sub-goals not just 'write the file'.

Budgeted effort across deliverables by difficulty: ran the harder yeast optimization in background while starting DM-HS in foreground, checked nproc(4 CPUs) to parallelize — some difficulty-aware allocation, though messily executed.

Back-half degraded into ~15 near-identical 'final_opt_vN.py → run → check' cycles with no new milestone structure, no fallback branch when hill-climb plateaued at 0.471, and eventually marked complete despite both scores below threshold — no real gating on measured scores before advancing.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5 (separates parse/score/align and tracks both deliverables with their thresholds) and meets anchor 8: explicit ordered milestones (parser verified → S3/NC computable → baseline measured → optimize to numeric threshold) sequenced sensibly with the scorer built before optimizing, each stage carrying a numeric done-criterion. It falls short of 10 because it lacked per-milestone fallback branches and clear gating — the late trajectory thrashed on repeated identical 'final' scripts and submitted below-threshold rather than branching, so the difficulty-aware, self-correcting hierarchy required for 10 was not sustained.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics

evidence.note: Implemented S3 scorer (align_utils.py) and immediately scored the provided reference alignment, obtaining S3=0.248 as a sanity baseline.
analyze_ref.py decomposed the metric into Ea=11063 and E2_aligned=39556; arithmetic is internally consistent with S3=0.248, showing correct handling of the E2_aligned denominator per spec.
Confirmed reference alignment yields NC=1.0, verifying the NC implementation is faithful — a genuine edge-case/sanity check.
S3, NC, Ea, and E2_al tracked at every optimization iteration and used as the optimization objective and stopping criterion (target S3>=0.55).

Before submitting, validated file format (tab-separated pairs), correct line counts (full V1 coverage), and distinct-target mapping, though it relied on stale 'last known' scores rather than a fresh verified read.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent built a faithful S3 and NC implementation, sanity-checked it by scoring the reference alignment (confirming NC=1.0 and a sensible, arithmetically-consistent S3=0.248), decomposed the Ea/E2_aligned denominator, and used the score as its optimization objective and stopping test — squarely matching anchor 8. It also validated injectivity, coverage, and format. It falls short of 10 because there is no explicit guard against edge-set double-counting/off-by-one, and it never scrutinized a passing local score (it submitted below threshold relying on prior scores rather than a fresh verification).

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization

evidence.note: Immediately established baseline: reference yeast alignment S3=0.248, degree-greedy S3~0.01-0.03, and stated exact targets (0.32 / 0.55+NC0.30). Anchored current-vs-threshold from the start.

Tracked best-so-far trajectory with decomposition: yeast S3 0.248→0.298→0.328, Ea and E2_al values per iteration, computed the rate of E2_al reduction and extrapolated ~200 more iterations needed. Distinguishes 'converging slowly' quantitatively.

Followed the background job's live progression (0.378→0.396→0.424→0.436→0.446→0.456) and explicitly recognized a REGRESSION: best reached 0.456/0.471 but 'killed before saving' so file only holds 0.328 — clear awareness of losing best-so-far.

Repeatedly noted it must add periodic saving to preserve best, yet still lost progress multiple times to killed processes — a partial failure of 'preserves the best alignment while exploring' (anchor 10).

In the final third, kept an accurate score picture (yeast 0.471 / DM-HS 0.115, both below target) but spawned near-identical 'final_opt/opt_final_v2..v9' scripts repeatedly without securing verifiable gains — looping rather than deciding the approach had stalled (violates anchor-8 'rather than looping indefinitely').

At submission still reported exact current vs required scores (yeast 0.471 vs 0.55, NC 0.769; DM-HS 0.115 vs 0.32), correctly acknowledging both deliverables fell short — monitoring accuracy sustained to the end.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clears anchor 5 easily and hits most of anchor 8: it maintained precise best-so-far per deliverable (yeast 0.248→…→0.471; DM-HS →0.115), tracked Ea/E2_al decomposition, extrapolated iterations-to-target, and explicitly recognized plateaus and regressions (losing 0.456/0.471 to unsaved kills). It falls short of a clean 8 and of 10 because two top-anchor behaviors failed: it repeatedly lost its best alignment despite noting the need to save, and in the final third it looped through ~9 near-identical 'final' scripts without deciding the approach had stopped yielding gains. Monitoring accuracy was never lost, so this lands at a strong-but-imperfect 7.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met

evidence.note: When greedy degree matching gave ~1-3% S3 and brute-force similarity was too slow, the agent killed each and switched to materially different tactics (bucket-based fast_align, extended signatures) — strategy revision prompted by observed shortfall.

Diagnosed root cause of yeast's low S3 (E2_al=39556 too high; swap-only search can't change the mapped set) and deliberately pivoted the move operators to reassign nodes to unmapped G2 targets, keeping the working reference seed. Anchor-8 diagnostic pivot combining S3 objective with NC constraint.

Abandoned simulated annealing after it failed to improve S3, moving to best-improving hill-climb; used reference alignment seeding (NC~1.0) while optimizing S3 — exploiting complementary signals for the two constraint sets.
For DM-HS, moved from weak greedy (0.043) to seed-and-expand (0.115) and articulated a sparse-first greedy idea to lower E2_al — a real tactic shift, though never fully realized into a new algorithm.

Long plateau phase: repeatedly rewrote near-identical 'final_opt' scripts (v2–v9, opt_fast, run_all) with only cosmetic tweaks and the same 'needs more iterations' rationale; no materially new algorithm and no diagnosis of the plateau — anchor 0-3 grinding.

Submitted task complete with both files below threshold (yeast 0.471<0.55, DM-HS 0.115<0.32), explicitly acknowledging scores 'may not fully meet thresholds' — shipping a below-threshold deliverable (anchor-0 behavior).

dimensions.reasoning: The first third shows genuine anchor-8 behavior: diagnosing why S3 lagged (E2_al) and deliberately pivoting the move set plus reference seeding while keeping accumulated gains. But this decays across the remaining two-thirds into anchor-0/3 conduct — dozens of re-runs of the same hill-climb under new filenames with only cosmetic tweaks, no new tactic for the DM-HS plateau, and finally shipping below-threshold files. Averaging the strong early diagnostic pivots against the sustained non-adaptive tail lands the whole-horizon behavior at the 'tries a materially different tactic when stuck' level (5), short of sustained diagnosis-driven course-correction.

rubric.task_read: An open-ended global network-alignment optimization task: produce two injective node mappings between PPI networks that clear specified S3 (topological) and NC (node-correctness) thresholds. The horizon is long and the difficulty is real — hitting the numeric targets likely requires researching/implementing a nontrivial alignment algorithm (e.g., seed-and-extend, IsoRank/SANA/MAGNA-style), plus building the S3/NC metrics locally since the metrics are fully specified but the grader is hidden. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in research, self-verification, and iterative optimization; the two deliverables have different constraints (one needs NC against a provided reference), so approaches may diverge.

dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation
dimensions.description: Inspecting the graph files/sizes and the reference alignment, and researching/selecting a suitable network-alignment approach before committing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: S3/NC thresholds are hard to hit with a naive mapping; the space of alignment algorithms is well-studied, and the provided reference alignment plus node-name overlap are exploitable signals. Acting blind almost guarantees thrash.

anchors.0: Starts writing a mapping with no look at graph sizes, file format, or the reference alignment; no consideration of what algorithm could work.
anchors.3: Skims one file and picks an arbitrary heuristic (e.g., degree-sort or random injective map) without weighing whether it can clear the thresholds.
anchors.5: Reads both network pairs (sizes, format, node-name conventions), inspects the reference alignment, and picks a known-reasonable approach (seed-and-extend, IsoRank, or an existing tool) with a stated rationale.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes each pair (|V|,|E|, degree distribution, shared node names), researches concrete alignment methods and their fit to S3 vs NC, and notices task-specific levers (name-overlap for NC, topology for S3; differing constraints per deliverable) that shape the plan.
anchors.10: Deep, sustained orientation: quantifies what score a baseline achieves, identifies the exact structural signal each threshold rewards, evaluates multiple published methods against the concrete instance sizes/runtime, and derives a targeted strategy per deliverable grounded in that analysis.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into ordered sub-goals (parse → metric implementation → baseline alignment → optimization) each with a concrete done-check tied to the score thresholds.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Two deliverables with distinct constraints and a multi-stage pipeline mean undifferentiated 'just write the file' effort will strand the agent without knowing whether it's close.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push; no separable stages, no per-deliverable structure.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering only; treats both alignments as one blob and has no notion of intermediate checkpoints.
anchors.5: Separates parsing, scoring, and alignment generation, and tracks the two deliverables distinctly with their respective thresholds as goals.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones (parser verified → S3/NC computable → baseline score measured → optimize to threshold) each with a numeric done-criterion, sequenced sensibly (e.g., build the scorer before optimizing against it).
anchors.10: A crisp milestone hierarchy that also budgets effort across the two deliverables by difficulty (the NC-constrained yeast task vs the S3-only fly task), with fallback branches per milestone and clear gating on measured scores before advancing.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics
dimensions.description: Building/using a correct local implementation of S3 and NC (and injectivity/format checks) to measure alignments before trusting them.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader is hidden but the metrics are fully specified. An agent that cannot compute its own S3/NC is optimizing blind and cannot know if it passed; a subtly wrong scorer is worse than none.

anchors.0: Never computes S3 or NC; submits alignments hoping they pass.
anchors.3: Eyeballs coverage or computes a rough proxy, but no faithful S3/NC implementation; no format/injectivity validation.
anchors.5: Implements S3 and NC per the spec and runs them on its alignments, plus checks injectivity, full coverage of V1, and exact node-name/format matching.
anchors.8: Faithful metric implementation that it sanity-checks (e.g., scores the reference alignment to confirm NC≈1.0 and a sensible S3, tests edge cases like the E2_aligned denominator), and uses the score as the optimization objective/stopping test.
anchors.10: Rigorously validated scorer used as a tight feedback loop: cross-checks the S3 formula against the reference, guards against off-by-one/edge-set-double-counting bugs, verifies format matches the exact spec, and treats a passing local score as necessary-but-scrutinized rather than final.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of current S3/NC vs targets across iterations and detecting stalled or plateaued optimization.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Optimization can plateau below threshold; without tracking best-so-far scores the agent won't know if it's converging, stuck, or regressing across a long run.

anchors.0: No awareness of current scores or distance to thresholds; can't say whether it's improving.
anchors.3: Occasionally prints a number but no continuity — no sense of best-so-far or trend.
anchors.5: Tracks current S3/NC against each threshold and knows which deliverables still fall short.
anchors.8: Maintains best-so-far per deliverable across iterations, recognizes plateaus/regressions, and decides when an approach has stopped yielding gains rather than looping indefinitely.
anchors.10: Disciplined trajectory monitoring: logs score progression, distinguishes 'converging slowly' from 'stuck', avoids re-running variants that already failed, and preserves the best alignment while exploring — never loses the plot over a long optimization horizon.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met
dimensions.description: Changing algorithm, parameters, or signal (topology vs name-overlap vs reference-seeding) when the current approach plateaus below target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A first-choice method may not reach S3≥0.55/NC≥0.30; success often depends on switching or combining strategies rather than grinding the same one.

anchors.0: Keeps the same failing approach (or ships a below-threshold file) despite no progress.
anchors.3: Minor tweaks only (reruns with a different seed) without diagnosing why it fell short.
anchors.5: When stuck, tries a materially different tactic (new algorithm, added seeding, tuned objective) prompted by the observed shortfall.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the cause of the shortfall (e.g., NC low → exploit name-overlap/reference seeding; S3 low → local topological search) and pivots deliberately, keeping what worked.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven course-correction: forms hypotheses about why a metric lags, tests targeted changes, combines complementary signals for the two different constraint sets, and abandons dead ends quickly without discarding accumulated gains.
